topic: Sold-out potatoes and a beeping self-checkout
title_jp: {売り切れ|うりきれ}とセルフレジ
context: Monday evening. アルちゃん wants to thank the 田中s by cooking them a Spanish tortilla, but the supermarket on the shopping street doesn't go to plan. He messages 健太 on LINE from the shop. Today: saying how you feel when things go wrong (and right) while shopping.

phrases.jp: {せっかく||going to the trouble|4}{来|き}たのに、{売り切れ|うりきれ|sold out|3}で{残念|ざんねん|a shame, disappointing|4}でした。
phrases.en: I came all this way, but it was sold out. What a shame.
phrases.note: せっかく〜のに = all that effort, for nothing. {残念|ざんねん}です is the polite way to show disappointment; with friends you'd say がっかりした.

phrases.jp: セルフレジで{失敗|しっぱい|messing up, failure|3}して、{恥ずかしかった|はずかしかった|embarrassed|4}。
phrases.en: I messed up at the self-checkout and it was embarrassing.
phrases.note: {恥|は}ずかしい = embarrassed or shy (in public, in front of someone). It's light and everyday, not 'ashamed' in a heavy sense.

phrases.jp: {使い方|つかいかた|how to use|4}がわからなくて、ちょっと{不安|ふあん|anxious, uneasy|3}でした。
phrases.en: I didn't know how to use it, so I felt a bit uneasy.
phrases.note: {不安|ふあん} = a vague unease about what's ahead; {心配|しんぱい} = worrying about something or someone specific.

phrases.jp: レジ{袋|ぶくろ}は{有料|ゆうりょう|paid, costs money|3}だから、エコバッグを{持ち歩く|もちあるく|to carry around|3}ことにした。
phrases.en: Plastic bags cost money, so I've decided to carry an eco bag around.
phrases.note: Since 2020 shop bags cost a few yen. At the till you'll hear レジ{袋|ぶくろ}はご{利用|りよう}ですか？ (Do you need a bag?) — answer {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です to say no.

phrases.jp: {店員|てんいん|shop staff|4}さんが{優|やさ}しくて、ほっとしました。
phrases.en: The shop assistant was kind, so I was relieved.
phrases.note: ほっとする = the tension leaves you: relieved. Add さん to {店員|てんいん} when you talk about them; calling out to staff, say すみません.

dialogue_setting: A LINE chat at about 17:40: アルちゃん is standing by the supermarket exit on the shopping street, 健太 is on a quiet reception shift at Guesthouse Kaze.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {健太|けんた}、ちょっと{聞|き}いて！{田中|たなか}さんたちに{お礼|おれい|thanks, a thank-you|4}がしたくて、{今夜|こんや}スペインのトルティーヤを{作|つく}ることにした！
dialogue.en: 健太, listen! I wanted to thank the 田中s, so I've decided to make them a Spanish tortilla tonight!

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: {ええやん||(Kansai) = いいじゃん, nice!|2}！アルちゃん{料理|りょうり}できるんや。で、なんでそんな{焦って|あせって|to be flustered, rushed|3}んの？ｗ
dialogue.en: Nice! So you can cook, アルちゃん. So why so flustered? lol

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: スーパー{行|い}ったら、じゃがいもが{全部|ぜんぶ}{売り切れ|うりきれ|sold out|3}で、めっちゃ{がっかり||disappointed|4}した…。しかもセルフレジがピーピー{鳴って|なって|to ring, beep|3}、{店員|てんいん|shop staff|4}さんが{来|き}ちゃって{恥ずかしかった|はずかしかった|embarrassed|4}
dialogue.en: I went to the supermarket and the potatoes were all sold out. So disappointing… And then the self-checkout kept beeping and a staff member came over. So embarrassing.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: セルフレジ{あるある||(slang) a classic, happens to everyone|3}やｗ {気|き}にせんでええって。てか、{田中|たなか}さんち{農家|のうか|farming family|2}やん？じゃがいもぐらいあるやろ
dialogue.en: Classic self-checkout moment lol. Don't worry about it. Anyway, the 田中s are farmers, right? They'll have potatoes, surely.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: あ、{確かに|たしかに|true, indeed|4}！じゃあ、{恵子|けいこ}さんに{聞|き}いてみることにする。{卵|たまご}と、2{割引|わりびき|discount|3}の{玉ねぎ|たまねぎ|onion|4}だけ{買|か}って{帰|かえ}るね
dialogue.en: Oh, true! Then I'll ask 恵子さん. I'll just buy eggs and some 20%-off onions and head home.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: それがええわ。{失敗|しっぱい|messing up, failure|3}しても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}。{恵子|けいこ}さんら、{絶対|ぜったい|definitely|4}{喜ぶ|よろこぶ|to be happy, pleased|3}で
dialogue.en: Good call. Even if it flops, it's fine. 恵子さん and the others will definitely be happy.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: ありがとう。ちょっと{不安|ふあん|anxious, uneasy|3}だったけど、{安心|あんしん|relief, peace of mind|4}した（スタンプ：うさぎがペコリ）
dialogue.en: Thanks. I was a bit anxious, but now I feel better (sticker: bunny bowing)

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: {今度|こんど}{俺|おれ}にも{作|つく}ってや！{大阪|おおさか}のお{好み焼き|このみやき|okonomiyaki|4}と{勝負|しょうぶ|a showdown, contest|3}やｗ
dialogue.en: Make me one next time too! It'll be a showdown with Osaka okonomiyaki lol

grammar.form: {辞書形|じしょけい}: + ことにする ({作|つく}る → {作|つく}ることにする) · ない{形|けい}: + ことにする ({買|か}う → {買|か}わないことにする) · decided: ことにした ({聞|き}いてみることにした) · a rule you keep: ことにしている ({毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}ることにしている)
grammar.explanation: Use it when you yourself make a choice: ことにした = I've decided (done), ことにする = I'll go with that (deciding right now), ことにしている = a personal rule you stick to. The classic mix-up is ことになる (the next point), where the decision comes from others or circumstances: {転勤|てんきん}することになった sounds like the company decided, not you.

examples.jp: {健康|けんこう|health|3}のために、お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}まないことにしました。
examples.en: For my health, I've decided not to drink.

examples.jp: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}は、スマホを{見|み}ないことにしている。
examples.en: I make a rule of not looking at my phone before bed.

examples.jp: {雪|ゆき}がひどいから、{旅行|りょこう}は{来月|らいげつ}にすることにした。
examples.en: The snow is bad, so we decided to do the trip next month.

quiz.question: {雨|あめ}だから、{今日|きょう}は{出|で}かけない＿＿。
quiz.en: It's raining, so I've decided not to go out today.
quiz.explain: It's your own decision, so ことにした. ことになった = it was decided for you; ようにした = made an effort to; ことがある = sometimes happens.

kanji.where: Red or yellow stickers on bento, sushi and fresh food in the supermarket, usually from about 7 p.m. until closing.
kanji.related: Smaller discounts are written in tenths: 2{割引|わりびき} = 20% off, 3{割引|わりびき} = 30% off.
kanji.breakdown: {半額|はんがく}: 半 half + 額 amount (of money) → 'half the price'.

tip.title: 割 counts in tenths, not percent
tip.body: Supermarket stickers use tenths: 1{割引|いちわりびき} is 10% off, 3{割引|さんわりびき} is 30% off, and {半額|はんがく} is half price. People talk this way too: それ、2{割引|にわりびき}だった！ The same kanji is in {割り勘|わりかん} (splitting the bill), so watch for it at the izakaya.

challenge.prompt: {恵子|けいこ}さん sees your shopping bag in the kitchen and asks: 「あら、{何|なに}を{作|つく}るの？」 Tell her what you've decided to make and how you feel about it, using 〜ことにしました.
challenge.hint: お{礼|れい}に · スペインの{料理|りょうり} · ちょっと{不安|ふあん|anxious|3}だけど
challenge.model_answer: お{礼|れい|thanks|4}に、スペインのトルティーヤを{作|つく}ることにしました。ちょっと{不安|ふあん|anxious, uneasy|3}ですけど、{楽|たの}しみです！
challenge.explanation: お{礼|れい}に = as a thank-you. {作|つく}ることにしました is your own decision in polite past (ことにしました), right for talking to your host's wife. ちょっと{不安|ふあん}ですけど、{楽|たの}しみです puts the worry first and the positive feeling last, which sounds warm and modest.

vocab.note: お{礼|れい}に〜 = as a thank-you; お{礼|れい}を{言|い}う = to say thanks.

vocab.en: to be flustered, in a rush
vocab.note: {焦|あせ}った！ = 'that was close / I panicked'. Very common in speech.
On signs often 売切 or {品切れ|しなぎれ}.
Phones, alarms, bells: {電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}ってる (your phone's ringing).
Opposite: {無料|むりょう} (free of charge).

extras.title: Supermarket signs
extras.title_jp: スーパーの{表示|ひょうじ}
extras.intro: What you'll read on shelves and stickers in any Japanese supermarket.

items.note: Evening stickers; the boxes go fast.

items.jp: {本日|ほんじつ|today (formal)|2}の{特売|とくばい|special sale|2}
お{一人様|ひとりさま|per person (polite)|2}1{点|てん}まで

items.note: Next to it you'll often see the {産地|さんち|place of origin|2}: {長野県産|ながのけんさん|from Nagano|2}.
Same idea as {売り切れ|うりきれ|sold out|3}, a bit more formal.

extras.title: When shopping goes wrong
extras.title_jp: こんな{時|とき}の{気持|きも}ち
extras.intro: Short, real reactions for small daily disasters.

items.note: Light, for small things like a sold-out item.
When you just missed something: the last one sold a minute ago.

items.jp: {気まずかった|きまずかった|awkward|3}。
{助かった|たすかった|that saved me|4}！
items.en: You saved me! / What a help!
items.note: Thanks for help that came at the right moment.

extras.title: 健太's Kansai-ben
extras.intro: The Osaka forms in today's chat, with standard Japanese.

items.en: = {気|き}にしなくていい (don't worry about it)
items.note: せん = しない, ええ = いい.
Sentence-final で works like よ.
